### `delete_agent`

Hard-destroy an AI agent. Cascades children (executions/conversations/messages/skills/etc) via dependent:destroy. For FKs without dependent: (mcp_sessions, ralph_loops.default_agent_id, team memberships, telemetry, learnings, messages, a2a tasks, etc), if reassign_to_agent_id is given those rows are repointed to it; otherwise they are deleted. Irreversible.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::AgentManagementTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.execute

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `agent_id` | string | Yes | Agent UUID, slug, or name to destroy |
| `reassign_to_agent_id` | string | No | Agent UUID, slug, or name to repoint un-cascaded FKs to. If omitted, those rows are deleted. |

| `description` | string | No | Override description on the clone |
| `category` | string | No | Override category on the clone |
| `system_prompt` | string | No | Override system prompt on the clone |
| `commands` | array | No | Override commands array on the clone |
| `tags` | array | No | Override tags array on the clone |

- **Permission**: ai.skills.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `skill_id` | string | Yes | Skill ID to delete |

| `skill_id` | string | Yes | Skill ID |
| `enabled` | boolean | Yes | Set to true or false |

### `attach_skill_to_agent`

Bind a skill to an agent — adds an Ai::AgentSkill row that lets the agent invoke the skill. Idempotent: re-attach updates priority/is_active.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SkillTool`
- **Permission**: ai.skills.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `skill_id` | string | Yes | Skill UUID or slug |
| `agent_id` | string | Yes | Agent UUID, slug, or name |
| `priority` | integer | No | Priority order (default 0) |
| `is_active` | boolean | No | Active flag (default true) |

### `detach_skill_from_agent`

Unbind a skill from an agent — destroys the Ai::AgentSkill row.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SkillTool`
- **Permission**: ai.skills.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `skill_id` | string | Yes | Skill UUID or slug |
| `agent_id` | string | Yes | Agent UUID, slug, or name |

## AI Safety & Autonomy

### `emergency_halt`

Emergency halt ALL AI activity for the account. Cancels running executions, pauses schedules, blocks LLM calls, and demotes all agents to supervised tier.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::KillSwitchTool`
- **Permission**: ai.kill_switch.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `reason` | string | No | Reason for the emergency halt |

### `emergency_resume`

Resume AI activity after an emergency halt. 'full' mode restores agent trust tiers and schedules from pre-halt snapshot. 'minimal' mode only lifts the suspension.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::KillSwitchTool`
- **Permission**: ai.kill_switch.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mode` | string | No | Resume mode: 'full' (restore snapshot, default) or 'minimal' (lift suspension only) |

## Activity Monitoring

### `get_activity_feed`

Get a unified activity feed of recent missions, conversations, execution events, and errors across the platform

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `hours` | integer | No | Lookback window in hours (default 24, max 168) |
| `limit` | integer | No | Max items per category (default 10, max 50) |

### `get_mission_status`

Get mission status. Without mission_id: all in-progress missions with approval gates. With mission_id: full mission details.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | No | Specific mission ID for full details (omit for overview) |

### `get_notifications`

Get notifications for the current user. Defaults to active+unread (default 10, max 50). Filterable by category, type, source_type, before timestamp, or unread_only=false to include read.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `limit` | integer | No | Max notifications to return (default 10, max 50) |
| `category` | string | No | Filter by category (e.g. ai, system, security) |
| `type` | string | No | Filter by notification type (e.g. autonomy_approval_required, ai_concierge_message) |
| `source_type` | string | No | Filter by metadata.source_type (e.g. system_fleet, system_cve_responder) |
| `before` | string | No | Only return notifications created before this ISO8601 timestamp |
| `unread_only` | boolean | No | Restrict to unread (default true) |

### `dismiss_notification`

Mark a notification as read

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `notification_id` | string | Yes | ID of the notification to dismiss |

### `dismiss_all_notifications`

Dismiss all active notifications permanently (sets dismissed_at). Returns count of dismissed.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read
- **Parameters**: none

### `mark_all_notifications_read`

Mark all unread notifications as read (lighter than dismiss — still visible but marked as read). Returns count.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read
- **Parameters**: none

### `get_system_health`

Get a lightweight system health snapshot: active counts, approval queues, error rates, and provider status

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read
- **Parameters**: none

## Uncategorized

### `system_assign_storage_owner`

Set the owner of a StorageAssignment. For owner_kind=service_user, supply service_user_username — the platform looks up (or auto-allocates via Identity::UserAllocator) the matching ServiceUser. For operator/nobody/root, only owner_kind is required. Optional shared_group_groupname overrides the default anongid (the owner's primary group) for multi-service write-shared mounts. Triggers an automatic chown task on the storage provider node; the NFS export keeps using the OLD anonuid until the chown completes to avoid EACCES storms on consuming services.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemStorageOwnerTool`
- **Permission**: system.storage.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `storage_assignment_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the StorageAssignment whose owner is being set |
| `owner_kind` | string | Yes | service_user | operator | nobody | root |
| `service_user_username` | string | No | Required when owner_kind=service_user |
| `shared_group_groupname` | string | No | Optional override of anongid for shared-write mounts |

### `system_list_storage_assignments_by_owner`

List StorageAssignments filtered by owner_kind, service_user_username, chown_state, or node_instance_id. Use for ops audits like "which assignments still use owner_kind=root?" or "show me every chown that's stuck in failed across the fleet".

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemStorageOwnerTool`
- **Permission**: system.storage.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `owner_kind` | string | No | Filter by owner kind: service_user | operator | nobody | root |
| `service_user_username` | string | No | Filter by the owning ServiceUser's username |
| `node_instance_id` | string | No | Filter by the storage provider NodeInstance UUID |
| `chown_state` | string | No | complete | pending | running | failed | manual_required |

### `system_storage_chown_status`

Inspect chown state of a StorageAssignment — current state, previous_uid/gid (if in flight), task id, start/complete timestamps, recorded error.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemStorageOwnerTool`
- **Permission**: system.storage.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `storage_assignment_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the StorageAssignment whose chown status to inspect |

### `system_storage_chown_retry`

Re-dispatch a failed or manual_required chown. Resets chown_last_error and transitions back to pending — the after_commit dispatch hook then queues a fresh task. Pass force_complete: true as an escape hatch for cases where the operator has manually chowned the files (e.g. on an external NFS provider the platform can't reach) and wants to flip the assignment to complete without re-running.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemStorageOwnerTool`
- **Permission**: system.storage.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `storage_assignment_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the StorageAssignment whose failed/manual_required chown to re-dispatch |
| `force_complete` | boolean | No | Escape hatch: flip the assignment to complete without re-running (use after a manual chown) |

### `system_blast_radius`

Infrastructure blast-radius: given a fleet node (System::Node name, System::NodeInstance name, or a bare provider cluster-node token like "dna"/"rna"), derive what currently depends on it — SDWAN peers/VIPs/services/port-mappings, instance-pool membership, direct + cross-node storage assignments, and other node_instance_id FK dependents.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemBlastRadiusTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `node` | string | Yes | Fleet node identifier: a System::Node#name, a System::NodeInstance#name, or a provider cluster-node token (e.g. "dna") embedded in cloud_instance_id |

- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `certificate_id` | string | Yes | System::AcmeCertificate id (status must be valid) |

### `system_expose_service_publicly`

Expose a service to the public internet end-to-end: create/reuse an SDWAN VIP, port-map it on the hub, provision a TLS certificate for the hostname, and regenerate the reverse proxy.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_hostname` | string | Yes | Public FQDN to serve the service on (certificate CN) |
| `service_protocol` | string | Yes | http | https |
| `sdwan_network_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Network to host the VIP |
| `sdwan_hub_peer_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Peer acting as the DNAT hub |
| `vip_cidr` | string | Yes | Operator-supplied host CIDR for the VIP (typically /128 v6 or /32 v4) within the network's /64 |
| `backend_port` | integer | Yes | Backend service port to route public traffic to |
| `target_peer_id` | string | No | Sdwan::Peer hosting the backend (mutually exclusive with target_instance_id) |
| `target_instance_id` | string | No | System::NodeInstance hosting the backend (mutually exclusive with target_peer_id) |
| `tls_issuer` | string | No | ACME issuer (default letsencrypt-prod) |
| `challenge_type` | string | No | ACME challenge (default dns-01) |
| `dns_credential_id` | string | No | System::AcmeDnsCredential id (for dns-01) |

### `system_expose_service_local`

Expose a backend service locally at /svc/<slug> on the platform's own host(s), authenticated by the reverse proxy (ForwardAuth). Creates or updates the Sdwan::Service and enables its local-exposure facet. Approval-gated. For the public internet use system_expose_service_publicly instead.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_id` | string | No | Existing Sdwan::Service id to expose (omit to create from the fields below) |
| `slug` | string | No | URL slug for /svc/<slug> (required when creating) |
| `name` | string | No | Service display name (required when creating) |
| `protocol` | string | No | Backend protocol: https | http (default https) |
| `backend_vip_id` | string | No | Sdwan::VirtualIp id of the overlay backend (this or backend_host when creating) |
| `backend_host` | string | No | Static backend host/IP (this or backend_vip_id when creating) |
| `backend_port` | integer | No | Backend port (required when creating) |
| `auth_mode` | string | No | public | authenticated | scoped (default authenticated) |
| `required_permission` | string | No | Permission required for scoped mode |
| `required_group` | string | No | Group/role required for scoped mode |
| `strip_prefix` | boolean | No | Strip /svc/<slug> before proxying (default true) |
| `certificate_id` | string | No | System::AcmeCertificate id whose CN to mount under (default: account primary) |

### `system_acme_provision_certificate`

Provision (issue) an ACME TLS certificate for a hostname; the issued cert is stored as a System::AcmeCertificate.

- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `common_name` | string | Yes | Primary CN / FQDN for the certificate |
| `issuer` | string | Yes | letsencrypt-prod | letsencrypt-staging | internal-ca |
| `challenge_type` | string | Yes | dns-01 | http-01 | tls-alpn-01 |
| `sans` | array | No | Additional Subject Alternative Names (FQDNs) |
| `dns_credential_id` | string | No | System::AcmeDnsCredential id (required for dns-01) |
| `acme_email` | string | No | ACME registration contact email |

### `system_create_service`

Create an Sdwan::Service (identity + overlay backend). Does NOT expose it — use system_expose_service_local to publish it at /svc/<slug>, or system_expose_service_public_tcp for Path B public TLS-carrying TCP. edge_mode/client_auth may be pre-provisioned here; public_enabled itself is owned by system_expose_service_public_tcp / system_unexpose_service_public_tcp, not this action.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `slug` | string | Yes | URL slug (lowercase alnum + hyphen, <=64, not a reserved platform path) |
| `name` | string | Yes | Service display name |
| `backend_port` | integer | Yes | Backend service port (1-65535) |
| `protocol` | string | No | https | http | tcp | tls (default https) |
| `backend_vip_id` | string | No | Sdwan::VirtualIp id of the overlay backend (this or backend_host) |
| `backend_host` | string | No | Static backend host/IP (this or backend_vip_id) |
| `status` | string | No | active | disabled (default active) |
| `edge_mode` | string | No | Path B TLS-carrying TCP: passthrough | terminate (default passthrough; inert until public_enabled) |
| `client_auth` | string | No | Path B mTLS enforcement: none | required (default none; required needs edge_mode terminate) |

### `system_list_services`

List this account's Sdwan::Service records, newest first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `status` | string | No | Filter by status (active | disabled) |
| `local_enabled` | boolean | No | Filter by local-exposure state |
| `public_enabled` | boolean | No | Filter by public (Path B) exposure state |

### `system_get_service`

Fetch a single Sdwan::Service by id (scoped to this account).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Service id |

### `system_update_service`

Update an Sdwan::Service's identity + backend plumbing (name, protocol, status, backend, Path B edge_mode/client_auth). Exposure semantics (local_enabled, auth mode, and public_enabled) are NOT settable here. local_enabled is owned by system_expose_service_local; public_enabled (Path B) is owned by system_expose_service_public_tcp / system_unexpose_service_public_tcp — deliberately not settable through this CRUD action in either direction. Regenerates the reverse proxy when the service is locally and/or publicly exposed.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Service id |
| `name` | string | No | New display name |
| `protocol` | string | No | https | http | tcp | tls |
| `status` | string | No | active | disabled |
| `backend_vip_id` | string | No | New overlay backend VIP id |
| `backend_host` | string | No | New static backend host/IP |
| `backend_port` | integer | No | New backend port |
| `edge_mode` | string | No | Path B TLS-carrying TCP: passthrough | terminate |
| `client_auth` | string | No | Path B mTLS enforcement: none | required (required needs edge_mode terminate) |

### `system_delete_service`

Delete an Sdwan::Service. Regenerates the reverse proxy if the service was locally exposed (removing its /svc/<slug> route).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Service id |

### `system_unexpose_service_local`

Disable a service's local /svc/<slug> exposure (fail-safe off — no approval needed) and regenerate the reverse proxy. The Sdwan::Service record is kept; re-expose with system_expose_service_local.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Service id |

### `system_expose_service_public_tcp`

Enable a service's public (Path B) TLS-carrying TCP exposure via Traefik HostSNI routing — validates protocol tls, a resolvable host, and (under edge_mode terminate) a matching valid ACME certificate, then flips public_enabled on and regenerates the reverse proxy. Approval-gated; the sole owner of turning Path B ON (in either direction — see system_unexpose_service_public_tcp).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Service id (protocol must be tls) |

### `system_unexpose_service_public_tcp`

Disable a service's public (Path B) TLS-carrying TCP exposure and regenerate the reverse proxy. Approval-gated (unlike the fail-safe, no-approval system_unexpose_service_local) — the sole owner of turning Path B OFF; system_update_service refuses public_enabled in either direction.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemIngressTool`
- **Permission**: system.ingress.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Service id |

### `system_acme_get_certificate`

Fetch a single ACME certificate's non-secret detail (status, issuer, expiry, vault_paths_present). NEVER returns PEMs, private keys, or Vault secret values.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemAcmeTool`
- **Permission**: system.acme.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `certificate_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the ACME certificate to fetch |

### `system_acme_renew_certificate`

Renew an ACME certificate currently in status=valid. Drives valid → renewing → valid via Acme::CertificateManager.renew!. Returns the reloaded non-secret cert detail on success.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemAcmeTool`
- **Permission**: system.acme.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `certificate_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the ACME certificate to renew (must be in status=valid) |

### `system_acme_revoke_certificate`

Revoke a non-terminal ACME certificate via Acme::CertificateManager.revoke!. Drives any non-terminal status → revoked. Optionally records a revocation reason.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemAcmeTool`
- **Permission**: system.acme.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `certificate_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the non-terminal ACME certificate to revoke |
| `reason` | string | No | Optional ACME revocation reason |

### `system_acme_create_dns_credential`

Register a new ACME DNS-01 provider credential (Cloudflare, Route53, etc.). The provider API token in `credentials` is handed straight to Vault — NEVER stored on the model, logged, or returned. The result serializes only the public index (name, provider, status).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemAcmeTool`
- **Permission**: system.acme.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Yes | Human-readable name for the DNS-01 credential record |
| `provider` | string | Yes | DNS provider slug (cloudflare|route53|gcloud|digitalocean|hetzner|porkbun|ovh) |
| `credentials` | object | Yes | Provider-specific secret token fields (SENSITIVE — stored in Vault only) |
| `metadata` | object | No | Optional non-secret metadata stored on the credential record |

### `system_update_template`

Update mutable NodeTemplate fields. Accepts everything system_create_template accepts, so nothing set at create time is stranded: name, description, enabled, public, node_platform_id, admin_user, config. `config` REPLACES the stored hash rather than merging into it — read the current value with system_get_template first if you mean to add a key. Omitted fields are left untouched.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `template_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeTemplate to update (account-scoped) |
| `name` | string | No | New display name for the template |
| `description` | string | No | New free-text description for the template |
| `enabled` | boolean | No | Whether the template is enabled (selectable for new nodes) |
| `public` | boolean | No | Whether the template is shared/public rather than account-private |
| `node_platform_id` | string | No | UUID of a NodePlatform to retarget the template to |
| `admin_user` | string | No | Default admin username provisioned on instances built from this template |
| `config` | object | No | Template config hash (init_script, boot_mode, sdwan_network_id, …) — REPLACES the stored hash |

### `system_clone_template`

Clone a NodeTemplate, copying its module assignments wholesale. The reuse-first move after system_discover_templates finds a near-match: clone, then adjust with system_assign_module_to_template / system_update_template_module rather than rebuilding from scratch. A clone copies conflicts too, so any composition problem is returned under `composition_report` (each entry states its own severity) — the clone still succeeds, and that report is the baseline later assignments must accept.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `template_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the source NodeTemplate to clone (account-scoped) |
| `name` | string | No | Name for the new template (defaults to '<source name>-copy') |

### `system_create_module`

Author a new NodeModule. Same surface as REST create. Spec fields (mask/file_spec/package_spec/dependency_spec/protected_spec) take newline-joined glob strings or already-encoded arrays. Reuse-first: run system_discover_modules before authoring — a duplicate module is the failure this action makes cheap.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `name` | string | Yes | Module name (unique per account) |
| `node_platform_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodePlatform this module targets |
| `category_id` | string | No | UUID of the NodeModuleCategory |
| `variety` | string | No | Module variety (e.g. subscription, instance) |
| `description` | string | No | Free-text description |
| `enabled` | boolean | No | Whether the module is enabled |
| `public` | boolean | No | Whether the module is publicly visible |
| `priority` | integer | No | Composition priority (lower applies first) |
| `copy_path_id` | string | No | UUID of a module to copy paths from |
| `lock_spec` | boolean | No | Lock the spec fields against further edits |
| `init_start` | string | No | Init start command |
| `init_stop` | string | No | Init stop command |
| `init_restart` | string | No | Init restart command |
| `reboot_required` | boolean | No | Whether applying this module requires a reboot |
| `mask` | string | No | Mask spec — newline-joined globs or encoded array |
| `file_spec` | string | No | File spec — newline-joined globs or encoded array |
| `package_spec` | string | No | Package spec — newline-joined names or encoded array |
| `dependency_spec` | string | No | Dependency spec — newline-joined entries or encoded array |
| `protected_spec` | string | No | Protected-path spec — newline-joined globs or encoded array |
| `consent_budget_per_day` | integer | No | Daily ceiling on autonomous decisions for this module (policy; the consumed-count ledger is not settable here) |
| `config` | object | No | Arbitrary module config hash |

Update an existing NodeModule's mutable attributes. Accepts the same fields as system_create_module; absent fields are left untouched. Does NOT accept the consent-budget consumed-count ledger — that is maintained by the autonomy gate.

| `category_id` | string | No | Recategorize the module |
| `lock_spec` | boolean | No | Lock/unlock the spec fields |
| `init_start` | string | No | Init start command |
| `init_stop` | string | No | Init stop command |
| `init_restart` | string | No | Init restart command |

| `dependency_spec` | string | No | Dependency spec |

| `consent_budget_per_day` | integer | No | Daily ceiling on autonomous decisions for this module |
| `config` | object | No | Arbitrary module config hash |

### `system_find_node_with_gpu`

Find live node instances that expose a GPU/accelerator, optionally filtered by gpu_type, a minimum per-GPU VRAM (min_gpu_memory_mb), and a minimum GPU count. GPU is resolved from the instance's provider_instance_type SKU or its agent-reported config["gpu"] hint.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `gpu_type` | string | No | Filter to a specific GPU/accelerator type (case-insensitive, e.g. 'A100') |
| `min_gpu_memory_mb` | integer | No | Minimum per-GPU VRAM in megabytes the instance must have |
| `min_gpu_count` | integer | No | Minimum number of GPUs the instance must expose (defaults to 1) |

### `system_list_instance_types_by_gpu`

List provider instance-type catalog SKUs that carry a GPU, optionally filtered by gpu_type and a minimum GPU count. Use to pick a GPU SKU for provisioning.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `gpu_type` | string | No | Filter SKUs to a specific GPU/accelerator type |
| `min_gpu_count` | integer | No | Minimum number of GPUs the SKU must carry (defaults to 1) |

### `system_deploy_inference_server`

Deploy an inference runtime (ollama) onto a GPU node and make it consumable: assigns the gpu-<accelerator>-runtime + inference-ollama modules, registers an ollama Ai::Provider at the endpoint (active only once the endpoint answers a health probe — modules apply asynchronously, so re-deploy after the runtime is up to activate), and optionally publishes an SDWAN service offering. Targets a node by instance_id (must be live + GPU-capable unless force), or auto-selects via gpu_type/min_gpu_memory_mb. Pass endpoint_override to point at an existing ollama (e.g. for smoke).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | No | UUID of the target GPU NodeInstance; omit to auto-select via gpu_type/min_gpu_memory_mb |
| `gpu_type` | string | No | GPU/accelerator type to match when auto-selecting a target instance |
| `min_gpu_memory_mb` | integer | No | Minimum per-GPU VRAM (MB) when auto-selecting a target instance |
| `model` | string | No | Inference model tag to pull/serve on the ollama runtime |
| `endpoint_override` | string | No | Point the registered ollama provider at an existing endpoint URL instead of deploying (e.g. for smoke tests) |
| `sdwan_network_id` | string | No | UUID of an SDWAN network to publish the inference service offering on |
| `vip_cidr` | string | No | CIDR for the SDWAN virtual IP to front the published inference service |
| `accelerator` | string | No | Runtime accelerator family — selects the gpu-<accelerator>-runtime module (default nvidia) |
| `force` | boolean | No | Bypass the terminated/GPU gating on an explicit instance_id |

### `system_grant_instance_mcp_tools`

Grant an instance-agent the MCP tool-name glob patterns it may invoke on the platform MCP (default-deny: an instance can call nothing until granted). Patterns match the 'platform.<tool>' name, e.g. 'platform.system_*_read' or 'platform.health'. mode: 'replace' (default) or 'add'. The instance must have announced as a peer.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the instance (announced peer) to grant MCP tool access to |
| `tool_patterns` | array | Yes | Glob patterns matching 'platform.<tool>' names the instance may invoke (e.g. ['platform.system_*_read']) |
| `mode` | string | No | 'replace' (default) to overwrite the grant list, or 'add' to append |

### `system_grant_instance_peer_skills`

A2A: grant an instance-agent the peer skill-name glob patterns it may invoke on OTHER instances via agent-to-agent MCP (default-deny). Patterns match a peer's offered skill name, e.g. 'embed-*' or 'summarize'. mode: 'replace' (default) or 'add'. The instance must have announced as a peer.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the instance (announced peer) to grant peer-skill call access to |
| `skill_patterns` | array | Yes | Glob patterns matching peer-offered skill names the instance may invoke via A2A (e.g. ['embed-*', 'summarize']) |
| `mode` | string | No | 'replace' (default) to overwrite the grant list, or 'add' to append |

### `system_discover_peers`

A2A: list the online, operator-enabled agent peers in the account and the skills they offer (capability discovery). Pass instance_id to discover from a specific caller's perspective (excludes itself). Discovery does not imply call permission — the call is still gated by system_authorize_peer_call.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | No | Optional caller instance UUID to discover from its perspective (excludes itself) |

### `system_authorize_peer_call`

A2A: decide whether a caller instance may invoke a skill on a target instance via agent-to-agent MCP (three-gate, default-deny: caller granted + target online/enabled + target offers skill + same account). Returns { authorized, reason }. Consulted by the on-node A2A transport before relaying a call.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `caller_instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the instance attempting the A2A call |
| `target_instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the instance the skill would be invoked on |
| `skill` | string | Yes | Name of the peer skill the caller wants to invoke on the target |

### `system_launch_agent_fleet`

L3: launch an agent-fleet orchestration mission — dynamically provision a fleet of agent-instances, grant them L2 (platform-MCP) + L2.5 (A2A) capabilities, delegate subtasks (hybrid coordinator + peer sub-delegation), aggregate, and reap. Creates an approval-gated Ai::Mission (mission_type: agent_fleet) bound to the system_agent_fleet template and starts it; the operator approves the review_fleet gate before any instances are provisioned. fleet_spec: { size, source('provision'|'pool'), node_id, provider_region_id, provider_instance_type_id, pool_name, grant_mcp_tools[], grant_peer_skills[], member_skills[], subtasks[{id,skill}], delegation('central'|'a2a'|'hybrid'), reap }.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `fleet_spec` | object | Yes | Fleet orchestration spec: { size, source, node_id, provider_region_id, provider_instance_type_id, pool_name, grant_mcp_tools[], grant_peer_skills[], member_skills[], subtasks[], delegation, reap } |
| `name` | string | No | Display name for the agent-fleet mission |
| `objective` | string | No | Free-text objective/goal for the fleet mission |

### `system_agent_fleet_status`

L3: inspect an agent-fleet mission — returns status, current_phase, error_message, and a summary of the fleet (plan, member/assignment counts, aggregated report, per-member reap actions, reap_incomplete flag).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the agent-fleet Ai::Mission to inspect |

### `system_reap_agent_fleet`

L3: re-run reap for a failed/stuck agent-fleet mission — returns pool members, terminates provisioned members, disables their peers. Safe to retry; reports per-member actions and a reap_incomplete flag when any member fails to terminate. Pass force:true to reap a fleet whose plan disabled reaping.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the agent-fleet Ai::Mission to re-reap |
| `force` | boolean | No | Reap even when the fleet plan set reap:false |

### `system_mint_peer_capability_token`

A2A: mint an Ed25519-signed capability token proving caller_instance may invoke `skill` on target_instance via agent-to-agent MCP. GATED on the 4-gate A2A policy (PeerCapabilityService.authorize) — only issued if the call is authorized. The on-node A2A MCP server verifies the token's signature OFFLINE against the advertised public key (no per-call platform round-trip). Short-lived (default 5 min). Returns { envelope, signature, handle, public_key, expires_at, sub, aud, skill, jti }.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `caller_instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the instance the token authorizes to make the call (token subject) |
| `target_instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the instance the token authorizes the call against (token audience) |
| `skill` | string | Yes | Name of the peer skill the minted token authorizes |
| `ttl_seconds` | integer | No | Default 300; clamped to 1..3600 (MAX_TTL_SECONDS) — revocation propagates via the agents' capability_keys pull, so token lifetime is hard-capped |

### `system_list_isolation_tiers`

L0: list the isolation tiers an agent deployment can request (native | gvisor | kata | firecracker | vm) with their Docker runtime / K8s RuntimeClass mapping, isolation strength, overhead, and host requirements. Pass isolation_tier inside a fleet_spec (system_launch_agent_fleet) to select one (default native).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read
- **Parameters**: none

### `system_provision_instance`

Provision a new cloud instance for a node (asynchronous; returns task_id). Agents SHOULD send a stable operation_id per logical request — retries carrying the same operation_id reuse the in-flight instance instead of provisioning a duplicate.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `node_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the node to provision a cloud instance for |
| `provider_region_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the ProviderRegion to place the instance in |
| `provider_instance_type_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the ProviderInstanceType (SKU) to provision |
| `operation_id` | string | No | Stable idempotency key per logical provision request |
| `options` | object | No | Per-provider provisioning options passed through to the adapter |

### `system_terminate_instance`

Terminate an instance (cleanly destroys cloud resource + transitions to :terminated). Use system_destroy_instance to fully remove a registry row that has no live cloud resource.

- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

### `system_destroy_instance`

Hard-destroy a NodeInstance registry row, walking known FK dependents (sdwan_peers + sub-tables, system_bootstrap_tokens, system_node_certificates, system_node_modules, system_storage_assignments, billing_provisioning_usage_records, etc.). Use ONLY for ghost rows: cloud_instance_id is null OR the provider resource is already gone. Irreversible. Does NOT call the provider to destroy a live VM — pair with system_terminate_instance for that.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeInstance registry row to hard-destroy (ghost rows only) |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

### `system_upgrade_boot_image`

Trigger an in-place boot-image (UKI) upgrade on a NodeInstance to its platform's currently promoted disk image (campaign 019f505f). Queues an agent task that pulls + cosign-verifies the target UKI, writes the ESP, and reboots — reusing the /persist cert (no re-enroll). Refuses if the platform has no promoted image or cosign trust is not configured. No-op if already current.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeInstance to upgrade |
| `force` | boolean | No | Queue the upgrade even if the node already reports the promoted git_sha |

### `system_instance_hold`

Place an operator ops hold on a NodeInstance: blocks start/reboot/terminate while offline work happens on its disks, and enforces the block at the provider where supported. Records who placed it and why — an unattributed hold is indistinguishable from a bug later. Expiry alerts but never auto-releases; system_stop_instance and force do not override it.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeInstance to hold |
| `reason` | string | Yes | Why the hold is being placed, recorded on the instance for the next operator |
| `ttl_hours` | number | No | Advisory lease length in hours before the hold is reported expired (default 4) |

### `system_instance_hold_status`

Verify a NodeInstance's ops hold by reading provider state directly — never by attempting a start, which on a broken hold would start the very instance the operator needed stopped. Reports drift between what the platform recorded and what the provider actually enforces.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeInstance to check |

### `system_instance_release_hold`

Release an operator ops hold placed by system_instance_hold, clearing the platform-side flag and any provider-side enforcement.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the held NodeInstance to release |

### `system_assign_module_to_template`

Bind a NodeModule to a NodeTemplate (creates a TemplateModule join). Refuses the assignment when it would introduce an error-severity composition conflict (declared Conflicts: relation, or a second instance-variety module in one category) and names the modules involved; soft protected_spec overlaps come back under `warnings` without blocking. Assigning with enabled=false skips the conflict check, because a disabled join is not expanded onto any instance — enabling it later (system_update_template_module) is what runs the check. Separately, when the target template already carries LIVE nodes the assignment still succeeds but reports its blast radius under `blast_radius` (provisioned_node_count + reason) and records a `system.template_mutation` FleetEvent, because the change reaches those nodes on the template's next apply. Preview first with system_compose_preview_template.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `template_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeTemplate to bind the module to |
| `module_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeModule to assign to the template |
| `priority` | number | No | Compose order for this module within the template (higher first; default 0) |
| `enabled` | boolean | No | Whether the join ships (default true). false stages the assignment without expanding it onto instances — and skips the conflict check, since a disabled join cannot collide. |
| `config` | object | No | Per-template config overlay, deep-merged over the module's own config at expansion time |
| `recommends_override` | object | No | Recommends resolution for this join: { replace: [...] } to set the exact list, or { included: [...], excluded: [...] } to adjust the module's defaults |

### `system_update_template_module`

Update an EXISTING TemplateModule join in place: priority, enabled, config, recommends_override. This is the non-destructive way to take a module out of a template — set enabled=false rather than unassigning, because destroying the join nullifies source_template_module_id on every derived NodeModuleAssignment and permanently orphans them. Enabling a disabled join runs the same composition-conflict check as system_assign_module_to_template and refuses when it would introduce an error-severity conflict. Any edit to a join that ships (before or after the edit) on a template with live nodes reports `blast_radius` and records a `system.template_mutation` FleetEvent — disabling included, since that takes the module off live fleet. Omitted fields are left untouched; `config` and `recommends_override` REPLACE the stored hash rather than merging into it.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `template_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeTemplate holding the join (account-scoped) |
| `module_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the assigned NodeModule — the join is addressed by (template, module), matching system_assign_module_to_template |
| `priority` | number | No | New compose order for this module within the template (higher first) |
| `enabled` | boolean | No | false disables the join without destroying it (preserving priority/config and derived assignments); true re-enables it, subject to the conflict check |
| `config` | object | No | Per-template config overlay — REPLACES the stored hash |
| `recommends_override` | object | No | Recommends resolution ({ replace: [...] } or { included: [...], excluded: [...] }) — REPLACES the stored hash |

### `system_compose_preview_template`

Design-time composition preview for a set of NodeModules — the same analysis the Visual Template Composer shows. Resolves the full dependency closure (explicit picks PLUS transitive requires/recommends) and returns the serialized modules, detected conflicts, footprint estimate, dependency graph, and resolver warnings/errors. Read-only: persists NOTHING, creates no template. Use it before system_create_template + system_assign_module_to_template to see conflicts the assignment path would refuse.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `module_ids` | array | Yes | UUIDs of the NodeModules to compose (account-scoped). The operator's explicit picks — dependencies are resolved automatically and flagged auto_resolved in the response. |

### `system_discover_modules`

Reuse-first module discovery — describe a PURPOSE ('reverse proxy with TLS', 'metrics scraper') and get existing modules ranked by semantic similarity, with a confidence bucket. Run this BEFORE authoring a new module (the module-authoring runbook's reuse gate). Use system_list_modules instead when you already know the name or just want to browse by variety. Ranking is pure vector similarity over persisted embeddings — there is no keyword fallback, so an unavailable embedding provider fails loudly rather than returning misleading matches. The `coverage` field reports how much of the searched catalog is actually embedded: an empty result with unembedded > 0 means NOT INDEXED, not 'nothing exists' (run rake system:catalog:backfill_embeddings). The `seed_count` field reports how many ranked candidates existed beyond the page you received (capped at top_k x3) — seed_count > results.size means the catalog had more to say, so re-ask with a larger top_k.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `intent` | string | Yes | Free-text description of the capability/purpose the module should serve |
| `top_k` | integer | No | Max results to return (1-50, default 10) |
| `variety` | string | No | Restrict to a module variety: config | instance | subscription |
| `platform_id` | string | No | Restrict to modules for a specific NodePlatform |
| `include_disabled` | boolean | No | Include disabled modules in the search (default false) |

### `system_discover_templates`

Reuse-first template discovery — describe a WORKLOAD ('public web serving stack', 'nightly batch runner') and get existing NodeTemplates ranked by semantic similarity, with a confidence bucket. A template's embedding folds in its assigned modules' names and descriptions, so the match reflects what the template actually composes, not just its name. Same no-keyword-fallback and `coverage` semantics as system_discover_modules. The `seed_count` field reports how many ranked candidates existed beyond the page you received (capped at top_k x3) — seed_count > results.size means the catalog had more to say, so re-ask with a larger top_k.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `intent` | string | Yes | Free-text description of the workload the template should serve |
| `top_k` | integer | No | Max results to return (1-50, default 10) |
| `platform_id` | string | No | Restrict to templates for a specific NodePlatform |
| `include_disabled` | boolean | No | Include disabled templates in the search (default false) |

### `system_module_publish_target`

Preview where a CI publish for a module slug would land and whether the platform would accept it, without publishing anything. Resolves by name (the same rule ManifestImportService enforces) and flags when a DIFFERENT module holds the target OCI repo binding — drift to clear or rebind, not necessarily a blocker. ### `system_module_publication_integrity`

Detect artifacts that reached the OCI registry but were never recorded on the platform — a build that pushed + cosign-signed successfully, then failed to notify (bad token, wrong API base, unreachable platform, 422). Compares registry tags against recorded NodeModuleVersions. NOT a staleness sweep: source age is never consulted, so a module whose newest build predates its newest commit is normal and not reported. Omit module_name to check every module the platform believes CI publishes for (has a gitea_repo_full_name binding).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `module_name` | string | No | Restrict the check to a single module by name; omit to check all modules with a repo binding |

### `system_create_instance_pool`

Tune an existing instance pool: min_size/max_size/target_size, status, provider region/type, metadata. The reaper reconciles to the new sizes on its next tick. (Template is fixed at create time.)

- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| `min_size` | integer | No | New lower bound on pool size |
| `max_size` | integer | No | New upper bound on pool size |
| `status` | string | No | active | paused | archived |
| `provider_region_id` | string | No | UUID of the ProviderRegion to provision future members in |
| `provider_instance_type_id` | string | No | UUID of the ProviderInstanceType (SKU) for future members |
| `preferred_regions` | array | No | Ordered list of ProviderRegion UUIDs for cross-AZ HA spread (replaces the pool's list; empty array clears it back to single-AZ) |
| `metadata` | object | No | Pool metadata hash (e.g. reuse_without_reset) |

Initiate graceful drain on a NodeInstance: records drain intent + emits FleetEvent so observability tooling (and future autonomy reconcilers) can act. Workloads remain running; operator should call system_terminate_instance after relocation completes. Idempotent — calling twice updates drain_initiated_at.

| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeInstance to mark for graceful drain |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | No | Suggested workload-relocation window (default 600 = 10 min). Stored in metadata for observability; does not auto-terminate. |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

### `system_get_cve_exposure`

Fetch the exposure breakdown for a CVE — exposed modules + per-module assignment counts, account-scoped via CveExposure → NodeModuleVersion → NodeModule.

- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `cve_id` | string | Yes | Canonical CVE id (e.g. CVE-2026-12345) to compute account exposure for |

### `system_create_cve`

Manually inject a Cve row (typically for embargoed CVEs not yet in NVD, or for drill-mode runbooks). Idempotent via cve_id uniqueness — re-running updates fields. NOTE: Cve table is GLOBAL (not account-scoped) — created CVEs are visible to all accounts. Requires elevated system.fleet.autonomy permission.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `cve_id` | string | Yes | Canonical CVE id, format CVE-YYYY-NNNN (4+ digits). Drills should use high-numeric ids like CVE-2026-99001. |
| `severity` | string | Yes | critical|high|medium|low|unknown |
| `summary` | string | No | Short human-readable summary of the CVE |
| `affected_packages` | array | No | [{name: 'openssl', version: '<3.1.4'}, ...] |
| `published_at` | string | No | ISO8601; defaults to now |
| `reference_url` | string | No | URL to the CVE advisory / reference |
| `feed_source` | string | No | nvd|ghsa|manual (default manual) |

### `system_delete_cve`

Destroy a Cve row + cascade-delete its CveExposures. Used for drill cleanup. Cves are global; deletion affects all accounts. Requires elevated system.fleet.autonomy permission.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `cve_id` | string | Yes | Canonical CVE id (e.g. CVE-2026-12345) of the global Cve row to delete |

### `system_unassign_module_from_template`

Remove a NodeModule from a NodeTemplate (destroys the TemplateModule join). Inverse of system_assign_module_to_template. Idempotent — returns success even when the join doesn't exist. Removing a SHIPPING join from a template with live nodes reports `blast_radius` and records a `system.template_mutation` FleetEvent — it takes the module off every node on the template on next apply. Prefer system_update_template_module with enabled=false: destroying the join nullifies source_template_module_id on derived assignments and orphans them.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `template_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeTemplate to remove the module from |
| `module_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeModule to unassign from the template |

### `system_update_module_assignment`

Enable or disable a NodeModuleAssignment (per-(node, module) toggle). enabled=true enables the assignment; enabled=false disables it. The assignment row is preserved either way — disabling drops the module from neighbor union mounts / rsync_spec generation without losing priority/config. Mirrors the NodeModuleAssignmentsController enable/disable member actions. Idempotent.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `assignment_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeModuleAssignment to enable/disable (account-scoped via its Node) |
| `enabled` | boolean | Yes | true → enable, false → disable |

### `system_return_pooled_instance`

Return a claimed instance back to its pool. Default disposition is 'recycled': the member drains + terminates and the replenisher provisions a fresh one (no cross-mission data residue). Pools with metadata reuse_without_reset=true (same-trust-domain workloads only) instead re-mark the member 'ready' for reuse ('reused' disposition).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the claimed pool NodeInstance to return to its pool |

### `system_delete_instance_pool`

Destroy an empty InstancePool row. Errors when pool still has members — drain first via system_drain_instance_pool, then delete.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | UUID of the empty InstancePool to delete (account-scoped) |

### `system_module_mark_canary`

Mark a NodeModule as a honeypot canary (config['honeypot']['canary'] = true). Canary modules are decoys — any access triggers a high-severity FleetEvent via honeypot_access_sensor. Idempotent — re-marking is a no-op. RESTRICTED BY DESIGN: placing a decoy is an autonomy decision, so this takes the worker-only system.fleet.autonomy grant; clearing one via system_unmark_module_canary needs only system.modules.update.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `module_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the NodeModule to mark as a honeypot canary |
| `lure_kind` | string | No | Display label for the canary (default 'credential_store') |

### `system_deploy_platform`

Deploy a new Powernode platform. Two execution shapes: (1) call with no `mode` to receive a wizard-card payload describing the form fields the operator should fill in — the chat UI renders this inline; (2) call with full args (mode, name, template_slug, [parent_url, spawn_mode for federated]) to actually provision. Standalone = sovereign platform; federated = peers back with this platform via P6 spawn flow. Federated mode returns a single-use acceptance_token that must be captured immediately.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mode` | string | No | standalone | federated. Omit to receive the wizard payload. |
| `name` | string | No | Display name for the new deployment (required when mode is set). |
| `template_slug` | string | No | NodeTemplate to provision from (defaults to powernode-hub). |
| `parent_url` | string | No | Required for federated mode — reachable URL of THIS platform. |
| `spawn_mode` | string | No | Required for federated mode — one of managed_child, autonomous_peer, cluster_member. |
| `region` | string | No | Provider region to deploy the new platform into |
| `instance_size` | string | No | Instance size/SKU hint for the deployment's compute |
| `service_role` | string | No | Service role for the deployment (selects the workload profile) |
| `public_dns_hostname` | string | No | Public DNS hostname to assign to the new platform |
| `token_ttl_seconds` | integer | No | TTL (seconds) for the single-use federated acceptance_token |

### `system_create_volume`

Register a new ProviderVolume. For NFS, pass transport=nfs + nfs_server + nfs_export_path. For block, pass volume_type_id. The platform records the row; on-node mounting happens at attach time.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `name` | string | Yes | Display name for the new ProviderVolume |

| `nfs_server` | string | No | Required for transport=nfs — hostname or IP |

### `system_revert_storage_migration_binding`

Request the on-node agent re-point the consumer's canonical mount back to the SOURCE volume (inverse of cutover). Reachable from status=failed (any cutover-phase failure), or status=completed when promote_target_binding! silently failed (the half-cutover). Target data is left intact. Records intent only — the node does the actual mount work.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | UUID of the StorageMigration to revert |
| `reason` | string | No | Optional reason recorded in the migration's audit log |

### `system_cleanup_storage_migration`

DESTRUCTIVE — deletes the migration's target-side scratch artifacts only: the target_subpath partial copy + snapshot_subpath scratch + node transient mounts. NEVER touches source data, the source/target volume, or sibling subpaths. Reachable only from status=failed or status=cancelled (once preparing was reached). Explicit operator action — never auto-run on failure. Subject to a grace window (system.storage.migration.cleanup_grace_hours, SiteSetting/Account#settings-resolved, default 24h); pass immediate: true to override.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | UUID of the StorageMigration to clean up |
| `reason` | string | No | Optional reason recorded in the migration's audit log |
| `immediate` | boolean | No | Skip the cleanup grace window and clean up now |

### `system_revert_disk_image`

Roll a NodePlatform's disk image back to a prior publication — restores the target publication's file_object onto the platform (and un-soft-deletes it if the target was retired), then retires the previously-active publication. With publication_id, rolls back to that specific publication; without it, auto-selects the most recent prior publication (the newest retired one, else the newest published one that isn't currently active). Refuses purged publications (FileObject hard-deleted) and publications with no file_object. Wraps System::Executors::DiskImage::RollbackPublication — the same transaction the DiskImagePublicationsController#rollback :proceed path uses.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `platform_id` | string | Yes | System::NodePlatform id to roll back |
| `publication_id` | string | No | Target DiskImagePublication to restore. Omit to auto-select the previous publication. |

### `system_lease_ci_runner`

Lease an ephemeral Gitea Act runner from a builder pool: acquire a warm builder instance, correlate it to the Gitea runner it self-registered, and return the lease. The instance is recycled (terminate + backfill) on release so no state bleeds between jobs.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `pool_name` | string | No | Builder InstancePool name to acquire from (e.g. 'ci-builders-amd64'). One of pool_name/pool_id is required. |
| `pool_id` | string | No | Builder InstancePool id (alternative to pool_name) |
| `purpose` | string | No | generic | module_build | disk_image_build (default generic) — selects the publish-arrival signal the reconciler waits on before release |
| `workflow_run_id` | integer | No | Gitea workflow run id this lease serves (set by the build orchestrator; drives auto-release when the run completes) |
| `workflow_run_repo` | string | No | owner/repo of the workflow run (needed to poll run state when workflow_run_id is set) |
| `correlate_timeout` | integer | No | Seconds to wait for the runner to correlate before returning (default from SiteSetting; 0 = single attempt, the reconciler finishes async) |

- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `lease_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the CiRunnerLease to release (account-scoped) |
| `force` | boolean | No | Release even if the runner is currently busy (default false) |

### `system_dispatch_module_build_batch`

Plan + dispatch a native module-build batch for a base_sha..head_sha range: computes which modules need rebuilding (System::ModuleBuildPlannerService — or every module with force_all), creates the System::ModuleBuildBatch, and leases ephemeral module-forge builders to run each module's ci.module_build task (System::NativeModuleBuildOrchestrator#dispatch!). Returns the batch immediately — planning and the first dispatch pass are synchronous; build/sign/publish completion is tracked asynchronously via the batch's status (see system_list_tasks / system_get_task for the underlying ci.module_build tasks). This planner builds ONLY manifest-backed platform modules (those with a modules/<slug>/ tree); package-origin modules materialized from an upstream apt/rpm package build through a separate package-closure trigger and are never planned here even with force_all — the result lists any it dropped under excluded_modules[] (with a reason each) plus excluded_count, and system_refresh_package_module is how you rebuild those. Requires system.module_builds.dispatch, which core grants only to the system_worker role by design (leaked-token blast-radius bound) — agent and operator principals cannot invoke this action.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `base_sha` | string | Yes | Pre-push commit SHA (diff base) the planner compares from |
| `head_sha` | string | Yes | Post-push commit SHA (diff head); also the source of each build's short tag |
| `force_all` | boolean | No | Skip the diff and plan every module with a manifest (manual full rebuild / CVE-driven sweep). Default false. |
| `trigger` | string | No | push | manual | cve (default manual) — recorded on the batch for audit |
| `source_repo` | string | No | "<owner>/<repo>" the base_sha..head_sha diff is taken against (default: the ci_build_source_repo manifest repo). Pass the CORE repo (e.g. powernode/powernode-platform) for a core-change build so the planner diffs the tree the change actually lives in — diffing the wrong repo plans 0 modules. |

| `label` | string | Yes | Operator-supplied device label, e.g. 'phone' or 'work-laptop' |

### `system_sdwan_propose_federation_peer`

Propose a new federation peer. Status starts at 'proposed'. With generate_token: true (Phase 11b), generates a single-use acceptance token (plaintext returned ONCE) — Account A operator copies it out-of-band to Account B operator who pastes it into system_sdwan_accept_federation_peer.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `remote_instance_url` | string | Yes | Base URL of the remote Powernode instance to peer with |
| `remote_instance_id` | string | No | Optional identifier of the remote Powernode instance |
| `remote_account_id` | string | No | Optional identifier of the remote account on the peer instance |
| `remote_prefix_advertisement` | string | No | /48|/56|/64 ULA prefix the remote instance claims |
| `generate_token` | boolean | No | When true, generate a single-use acceptance token (Phase 11b token round-trip handshake). Plaintext returned ONCE — not recoverable. |
| `token_ttl_seconds` | integer | No | Token expiry window in seconds (default 7 days) |

### `system_sdwan_accept_federation_peer`

Transition a proposed federation peer to accepted. When the proposing operator generated a single-use acceptance token, pass it as acceptance_token — it is verified (digest match + not expired + single-use) before the transition is allowed. Sets signed_at + audit metadata and (for platform peers) chains into enroll. Returns the updated peer.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the federation peer to accept (must be in 'proposed' status) |
| `acceptance_token` | string | No | Single-use token from the proposing-account operator (from propose with generate_token: true). Verified against the stored digest; consumed on success. |

### `system_sdwan_update_federation_peer`

Update a federation peer's mutable fields. When `status` is supplied it is gated by the v1 transition matrix (FederationPeer#can_transition_to?) — disallowed transitions return an error. Mirrors the FederationPeersController#update permitted keys.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the federation peer to update |
| `status` | string | No | Target status — must be an allowed v1 transition from the current status |
| `remote_instance_url` | string | No | Base URL of the remote Powernode instance |
| `remote_instance_id` | string | No | Identifier of the remote Powernode instance |
| `remote_account_id` | string | No | Identifier of the remote account on the peer instance |
| `remote_prefix_advertisement` | string | No | /48|/56|/64 ULA prefix the remote instance claims |
| `signed_at` | string | No | ISO8601 timestamp marking when the peering was signed |
| `expires_at` | string | No | ISO8601 timestamp marking when the peering expires |
| `metadata` | object | No | Free-form metadata hash stored on the peer |

### `system_sdwan_federation_compose`

Stand up a federation overlay topology (hub-and-spoke OR full-mesh) across instances. Creates one Sdwan::Network, enrolls each member as a peer (hubs publicly_reachable), and compiles the per-peer WireGuard + FRR route-policy envelope (Sdwan::PeerEnroller + TopologyCompiler + RoutePolicyCompiler). Failures are collected, not short-circuited.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `network_name` | string | Yes | Display name for the new federation Sdwan::Network |
| `topology` | string | Yes | hub_and_spoke | full_mesh |
| `peers` | array | Yes | Member descriptors (1-200). Each: {node_instance_id (required), role: 'hub'|'spoke' (hub_and_spoke only; default spoke), endpoint_host_v6, endpoint_host_v4, endpoint_port, listen_port, lan_subnets: [cidr], bgp_route_reflector_client: bool} |
| `routing_protocol` | string | No | static (default) | ibgp — 'ibgp' enables FRR route-policy distribution |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | Plan only — no rows persisted |

### `system_multi_tenant_isolation`

Provision a fully-isolated SDWAN network slice for a single tenant: a dedicated overlay network with its own VRF + isolated iBGP RIB, a non-overlapping /64, default-deny nftables rules scoped to the tenant CIDR, an OVN logical switch, and tenant-CIDR OVN ACLs. SDWAN-native — no k8s NetworkPolicy, no VLAN. Approval-gated.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `tenant_key` | string | Yes | Stable slug-safe tenant identifier within the account (names the network/rules/switch/ACLs) |
| `network_name` | string | No | Display name for the tenant's Sdwan::Network (defaults to 'tenant-<tenant_key>') |
| `tenant_cidr` | string | No | Explicit tenant CIDR; when omitted the auto-allocated /64 is used (recommended) |
| `nb_db_endpoint` | string | No | OVN NB DB endpoint (e.g. tcp:127.0.0.1:6641) — required only when the account has no Sdwan::OvnDeployment yet |
| `sb_db_endpoint` | string | No | OVN SB DB endpoint (e.g. tcp:127.0.0.1:6642) — required only when the account has no Sdwan::OvnDeployment yet |
| `ovn_switch_name` | string | No | Override the OVN logical switch name (defaults to 'ls-tenant-<tenant_key>') |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | Plan only — no rows persisted |

### `system_service_discovery_compose`

Make a backend service discoverable across the fleet over the SDWAN overlay — provisions a Virtual IP (auto-advertised via iBGP for in-overlay discovery), publishes a VIP-backed federation service-catalog offering, regenerates local Traefik routes, and OPTIONALLY publishes a public DNS record (A/AAAA/CNAME) for internet-facing names. Approval-gated.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_name` | string | Yes | Human-readable catalog display name |
| `service_slug` | string | Yes | Lowercase-alphanumeric-hyphen slug — the catalog's natural key (also names the VIP) |
| `sdwan_network_id` | string | Yes | SDWAN network the VIP lives in |
| `backend_peer_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Peer hosting the service; seated as the VIP's primary holder (iBGP advertiser) |
| `backend_port` | integer | Yes | Port the backend service listens on (advertised in the catalog offering) |
| `vip_cidr` | string | Yes | Operator-supplied host CIDR for the VIP (a /128 v6 or /32 v4) within the network's /64 |
| `protocol` | string | No | Service protocol advertised in the catalog: https (default) | http | tcp | tls |
| `grant_scopes` | array | No | Default FederationGrant scopes subscribers receive (subset of read, write, admin, migrate). Defaults to ['read'] |
| `grant_ttl_days` | integer | No | Default grant TTL in days (>= 7) |
| `traefik_dynamic_dir` | string | No | Override for the Traefik dynamic-config directory |
| `public_dns` | object | No | INTERNET-FACING name only: { dns_credential_id, record_name, record_type? (A|AAAA|CNAME), record_content?, ttl? }. Omit for overlay-only discovery. |

### `system_sdwan_create_virtual_ip`

Create a Virtual IP. Static mode (anycast=false) = single primary holder + ordered failover. Anycast mode (slice 9c iBGP) = all holders advertise simultaneously. CIDR is typically /32 (v4) or /128 (v6).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `network_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the SDWAN network the Virtual IP lives in |
| `name` | string | Yes | Display name for the Virtual IP |
| `cidr` | string | Yes | Host CIDR for the VIP (typically /32 for v4, /128 for v6) within the network's /64 |
| `holder_peer_ids` | array | Yes | Ordered: first entry is primary holder when anycast=false. |
| `failover_holder_peer_ids` | array | No | Ordered failover candidates (non-anycast); head is promoted on failover |
| `anycast` | boolean | No | When true, all holders advertise simultaneously (slice 9c iBGP); default false |
| `description` | string | No | Free-form description of the VIP's purpose |
| `tags` | array | No | Optional list of tag strings applied to the VIP |
| `advertised_med` | integer | No | BGP MULTI_EXIT_DISC advertised for this VIP (default 0) |
| `advertised_local_pref` | integer | No | BGP LOCAL_PREF advertised for this VIP (default 100) |

### `system_sdwan_create_port_mapping`

Create a hub DNAT mapping. Exactly one of target_peer_id or target_virtual_ip_id must be set. The hub peer must be in the same network as the target.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `network_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the SDWAN network the mapping belongs to |
| `hub_peer_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the hub peer that listens for and DNATs the traffic |
| `name` | string | Yes | Display name for the port mapping |
| `listen_port` | integer | Yes | Port the hub listens on for inbound traffic |
| `protocol` | string | Yes | tcp | udp |
| `target_peer_id` | string | No | UUID of the target peer to DNAT to (mutually exclusive with target_virtual_ip_id) |
| `target_virtual_ip_id` | string | No | UUID of the target virtual IP to DNAT to (mutually exclusive with target_peer_id) |
| `target_port` | integer | No | Defaults to listen_port if omitted |
| `description` | string | No | Free-form description of the mapping |
| `enabled` | boolean | No | Whether the mapping is active (default true) |
| `rate_limit` | integer | No | Hardened DNAT tier (increment 6): max NEW CONNECTIONS per second (conntrack flows — the nat chain only sees each connection's first packet, so this throttles connection-establishment rate, not request/packet throughput). Omit for unrestricted (default). |
| `max_connections` | integer | No | Hardened DNAT tier (increment 6): max concurrent connections before excess are dropped. Omit for unrestricted (default). |
| `source_cidrs` | array | No | Hardened DNAT tier (increment 6): allow-list of source CIDR strings (v4 and/or v6). Traffic from any other source is dropped. Omit/empty for unrestricted (default). |

Pass rate_limit/max_connections as null or source_cidrs as [] to clear back to unrestricted. |
